citationTopicHierarchy.system: Nature citation topic / Nature Research Intelligence topics
citationTopicHierarchy.basis: Official breadcrumb links on the topic page; this is a separate scheme, not linked by assumed equivalence to Nature ontology nodes.
citationTopicHierarchy.countWarning: Nature Index topic trends explicitly cover articles across all publications, not only Nature journals or the selected subject channel.

coverage.selection: Purposeful connected subset around the seed article’s five Nature ontology subjects, with physics, chemistry, materials science, nanoscience, and selected related topics. Not a complete Nature subject taxonomy.
coverage.hierarchyBasis: Every graph edge is an explicit Browse broader subjects or Browse narrower subjects link on an official Nature Physics subject page. Broader/narrower is an editorial browsing hierarchy, not a historical lineage or proof of disciplinary causation.
coverage.nodeFacetBasis: Node facets such as property, phenomenon, material-family, method, and application/device are our non-exclusive reading aids. They must be labeled as editorial facets and must not be presented as publisher-supplied ontological types.
coverage.multiParentPolicy: Preserve every verified parent-child edge whose endpoints are in this selected graph. The same topic may have several parents. Other official parents outside the selected graph are recorded in omittedHierarchyEdges.
coverage.countWarning: The selected Nature channels contain research beyond quantum materials. Their counts are channel publication counts, not a quantum-materials-only corpus, and overlapping subject counts must not be summed without article-level deduplication.
coverage.noInventedQuantumMaterialsNode: No official quantum-materials ontology node is asserted here. An interface may add a clearly marked editorial umbrella node and source its conceptual connections separately.
coverage.quantumConfinement: A direct /subjects/quantum-confinement/nphys probe returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-04; no Nature hierarchy node or count is invented for it. Quantum dots remains a verified materials/structure node; a confinement mechanism link would require a separately sourced editorial relation.
